short: Germany, Italy, and Japan signed a mutual defense treaty, formally creating the Axis powers.
full:
On 27 September 1940, representatives of Germany, Italy, and Japan signed the Tripartite Pact in Berlin. The agreement formalized the alliance between the three nations, pledging mutual political, economic, and military assistance if any signatory were attacked by a power not already involved in the European war or the Sino-Japanese conflict. It was explicitly intended as a warning to the United States to remain neutral.

The pact cemented the core of the Axis powers and linked the wars in Europe and Asia into a single global struggle. Several other nations, including Hungary, Romania, and Bulgaria, later joined the pact. While the alliance improved strategic coordination among its members, diverging national interests often limited their practical military cooperation throughout the war.
